prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on your goals (style, budget, scale, platforms). Below are the top options by use-case, with strengths so you can pick quickly.

Top picks by use-case

- Synthesia (or HeyGen / Movio)
  - Best for: professional AI presenters/hosted ads with lifelike avatars and multilingual voiceovers.
  - Strengths: realistic talking-heads, brand tuning, fast script → video.
  - Limitations: costlier, limited full-scene creative control vs. manual editors.

- Pictory
  - Best for: turning blog posts/long-form content into short social ads.
  - Strengths: automatic highlights, captions, stock footage, easy repurposing.
  - Limitations: less control for advanced motion design.

- InVideo / Promo.com / Canva (templates-driven editors)
  - Best for: fast social ads using templates and stock assets.
  - Strengths: huge template libraries, quick aspect-ratio exporting, simple branding.
  - Limitations: less “AI magic” for voice or avatars; template look can feel generic if not customized.

- Vidyo.ai / ClipSage
  - Best for: clipping long videos into multiple short ad/short-form variants automatically.
  - Strengths: automated highlight detection, multi-aspect outputs for testing.
  - Limitations: mainly for repurposing rather than creating from scratch.

- VEED / Kapwing
  - Best for: easy online editing with AI subtitling, text-to-speech, and collaboration.
  - Strengths: strong subtitle/branding tools and simple UI.
  - Limitations: fewer advanced templates than Promo/Canva.

- Spirable / Idomoo (enterprise)
  - Best for: highly personalized, dynamic ads at scale (1:1 personalization).
  - Strengths: integration with data feeds, campaign-level personalization, analytics.
  - Limitations: enterprise pricing, setup complexity.

- Runway / Synthesys / Adobe Firefly (experimental generative)
  - Best for: cutting-edge generative visuals or unique creative experiments.
  - Strengths: novel outputs and creative control.
  - Limitations: still evolving; may require manual polishing.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Platform: vertical short-form (TikTok/Instagram) vs. horizontal (YouTube) — need templates/aspect ratios.
- Creative style: live presenter/host, animated text + stock footage, repurposed clip.
- Scale: one-off ad vs. dozens of personalized variants.
- Budget: free/low-cost templates (Canva, InVideo) vs. paid avatar/enterprise (Synthesia, Idomoo).
- Speed vs. control: fully automated generation vs. manual editing flexibility.
- Localization: do you need multiple languages/voices?

My recommendation, by typical scenarios
- Fast low-budget social ads: Canva or InVideo.
- Repurposing webinars/blogs into ads: Pictory or Vidyo.ai.
- Ads with a talking human presenter (no filming): Synthesia or HeyGen.
- Large-scale personalized campaigns: Spirable or Idomoo.

If you tell me: what platform(s) you’ll run ads on, approximate budget, and the ad style you want, I’ll recommend 2–3 tools and a quick workflow to get your first ad done. Which are you targeting?
